equivalence_argument: With every B4 flag at its default (and the core registers no lever, so all are off), b4wave.train runs b3wave's trainer with no change to training. (1) build_rtc_augmenter_b4(args) returns build_rtc_augmenter_b3(args), the B3 augmenter object itself, and build_dataset_b4/build_augmenter_b4 are line copies of the b3wave builders with that factory. So the data path, the numpy/python/torch draws, describe(), meta_keys and the augmenter keys in config.yaml are b3wave's. Checks: levers_off_returns_b3_object, b4_config_equals_b3_config, train_dataset_levers_off_equals_b3, and train_items_bit_identical, where 3 real clips are bit-identical after load + augment + ffmpeg codec. (2) Even a forced RTCAugmenterB4 with no lever on is bit-identical to B3 on 200 clips without the codec plus 10 with fixed and 10 with random codec profiles, with the same stage_counts, and it never creates rng4. Its __call__ mirrors RTCAugmenter/RTCAugmenterB3 line for line, and _post_dsp returns the audio untouched without drawing. (3) No lever package or lever module is imported and no libopus is mapped, checked in a fresh process. (4) The model is b3wave's ModelSLSB3: keys are exact and logits match ModelSLS exactly on real dev clips (checks gpu, run on the CPU here). Optimizer, schedule, EMA, checkpointing, resume and pruning code is the unchanged copy. (5) build_parser() holds the same b3wave arguments, and parsing B2f's argv gives all 100 b3wave args unchanged (parser_reproduces_b3wave_on_base_argv). (6) Per-class telemetry runs only when a lever is on (track_by_class=bool(b4_levers)). Even when on, train_epoch losses and parameters are bit-identical (train_epoch_by_class_no_effect). The metrics.jsonl row gets 'b4' only when a lever is on. Bookkeeping-only differences: two header lines after 'b3wave: <v>' ('b4wave: <v>' from the scaffold, and 'b4wave sha256: <12>' required by the module contract) and three config.yaml keys (b4wave_version, module_sha256, b4_levers: []). The 'Epoch N/M TrainLoss', 'Epoch N LocalWF1' and 'Epoch N B3' lines are unchanged.
open_issues: Scaffold vs plan section 2.0: the plan says the 'b4wave: <version>' line replaces 'b3wave: <version>'. The scaffold keeps the b3wave line and adds the b4wave line after it; I kept the scaffold (the base header lines stay a subset and exploop's early check '^b4wave: ' matches). The module contract also adds 'b4wave sha256: <12>'.
Lever headers are printed only when a lever is on (plan section 2.0 / shared changes), not 'on or off' as the rd-implement skill words it: the plan wins.

scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py was built in core because it is shared, every lever lists it, and it needs no lever code. CLI additions beyond the plan's list: --run_pair (the arm's merge/final, derived by default; needed for condition (d) and the both-readouts outcome escape of O3.2), --lever (default from config.yaml b4_levers; needed for the O3.1 non-target rule), --summary (O3.3 provisional -> final). --halves B adds a half-B view; the verdict stays on the full set.

The O3.1 under-fit thresholds are derived from B2f's train.log (ep1 TrainAcc - 2 = 85.36; 1.5 x last TrainLoss = 0.0752, matching plan section 2.0). 'Heldout bona recall down' uses half_B sim_heldout_v1 recall_bona at the final readout vs B2f.

The 'B4 wave' argparse group is empty until the lever parts add their literal b4.add_argument('--aug_...') calls (exploop greps train.py for flags). The supervisor's --help flag check needs the lever flags, so STATIC will only pass after the lever parts.

One scratch toy-trainer invocation, given a 60 s tool timeout and malformed args, was moved to the background by the harness. The guard blocked pkill, so it ran to completion: the levers-off path twice in $TMPDIR, exit 0, CPU only. It was rerun correctly in the foreground.
overfit --lever <approved id> prints SKIP and exits 0 (no lever has params_added); the guard treats this target as a GPU check.
